summary: BHP Group is scheduled to release its full-year FY2026 results (year ended June 30) before markets open on August 18, 2026. Analysts expect EPS of $2.67 and revenue of $30.21 billion. In the HY26 update, copper contributed more than half of group EBITDA for the first time in the company's history, and BHP raised full-year copper production guidance to 1.9-2.0 million tonnes.
key_facts: BHP FY2026 results due Aug 18 before market open
Est. EPS: $2.67; Est. revenue: $30.21B
Copper >50% of group EBITDA in HY26 (first time in company history)
Copper production guidance raised to 1.9-2.0Mt for FY2026

headline: Moderna +76.8% year-to-date in 2026, one of sharpest large-cap biotech recovery trades despite 22% pullback from peak
summary: Moderna has emerged as one of the strongest large-cap biotech recovery trades in 2026, with shares up 76.8% year-to-date despite a recent approximately 22% pullback from recent highs. Strong pipeline data and improved commercial execution are cited as the primary drivers of the rebound, with analysts highlighting the stock's improving fundamental outlook and technical strength.
key_facts: Moderna (MRNA) +76.8% YTD in 2026
Down ~22% from recent peak (current pullback)
Pipeline data and commercial execution driving recovery
Characterized as one of sharpest large-cap biotech recovery trades of 2026

headline: Top oil and gas stocks surge on Middle East news in August 2026; XOM leads as energy outperforms all sectors
summary: Oil and gas stocks including ExxonMobil, Chevron, and EOG Resources continued to outperform all other sectors in August 2026 as Middle East tensions kept oil prices elevated. The Morningstar US Energy Index is up 33.74% year-to-date versus 10.43% for the broader market, with energy stocks appealing as both an inflation hedge and a direct beneficiary of the Iran war premium on crude.
key_facts: Energy sector +33.74% YTD vs market +10.43% YTD
Iran war premium sustaining oil prices above $80 WTI
Energy stocks function as inflation hedge and geopolitical hedge
Chevron: 39th consecutive annual dividend increase in 2026

headline: JPMorgan: sustained elevated Brent could depress H1 2026 global GDP by 0.6% annualized
summary: J.P. Morgan Global Research estimated that if Brent crude prices remained elevated through mid-year due to the Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, global GDP growth for H1 2026 could be depressed by approximately 0.6% at an annualized rate. The Iran war — which caused Brent to surge 10-13% to $80-82 early in the conflict — has reshaped global oil markets and disrupted supply chains in ways that extend well beyond oil into LNG and broader commodity trade.
key_facts: JPM: sustained elevated Brent could cut H1 2026 global GDP by 0.6% annualized
Iran war initially pushed Brent +10-13% to ~$80-82 in March 2026
Strait of Hormuz closure: largest supply disruption in oil market history
Brent holding near $88.50 as of Aug 17

headline: Markets price ~30% chance of September Fed hike after soft retail sales and consumer sentiment data
summary: Following the July FOMC hold at 3.50%-3.75%, markets have trimmed the probability of a September 25bp rate hike to approximately 30% after US retail sales fell 0.6% in July and UMich consumer sentiment dropped to 51.0. Chair Warsh's majority holds that more data is needed before acting; three dissenting hawks (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) continue to push for tightening. The September 15-16 meeting will be data-dependent.
key_facts: September rate hike probability: ~30% (CME FedWatch)
Down from ~62% in early August
Drivers of decline: July retail sales -0.6%, UMich sentiment 51.0
Fed funds rate: 3.50%-3.75%
Next FOMC: September 15-16
